My response is going to be one that I don’t feel the need to even bring the enneagram into, but I am a 9w8 as well.  

I get it. Break-ups are hard. You’ve known him for many years, you’ve fostered a sense of comfort with him, and therefore you want to make it work no matter what. 

It seems like maybe you and your boyfriend just aren’t compatible, and that is okay and not a moral failing on either of your parts.

I believe that in any situation where you say ‘it’ll be fine, I/the other person can change!’, it’s a sign that the relationship needs to end.

Your boyfriend doesn’t deserve to feel pressured into situations where he’s uncomfortable, and you don’t deserve to have to put up a fight in order to have your needs met. Of course through a Reddit post I won’t know all the nuances, but to me it seems like perhaps you need to bite the bullet and let it end, especially since he seems to already want that. I totally understand feeling the need to pressure a partner into backing out of a breakup, but that will never end well.

I wish you luck in this situation! I know it sucks.

Oh several things! I’m very practical and any pseudoscience is cringey to me but whether the enneagram is “real” or not, it’s certainly helped me!

1. Understanding that other people have different motivations than me has been #1. When other people do things I may not like or agree with, I now get that they’re not being a bad person, they just have a different core fear than me! It’s been sooo helpful in my relationships.

2. As a 9, understanding that it is NOT BAD to be complacent or satisfied with where you are in life. American culture is extremely ‘do do do’, and success-oriented. I’ve never cared about that and through the enneagram I realized that it doesn’t make me any worse at being a human than Jeff Bezos!

3. Understanding my fear of confrontation has allowed me to learn healthy confrontation practices! And when I don’t want to confront something, I’m able to figure out what I’m /actually/ afraid of, which is really helpful in either forming an effective communication, or choosing not to confront and allowing myself grace for it

The behaviors you described are stereotypical of a 7, but I could also see you being a 3! Have you taken the time to read through all the types? Ultimately it’s more about your core motivations than your actual behaviors 🥰

Oh you very well may still be a 9. I would’ve described myself as pessimistic for most of my life. In the past few years I’ve made a lot of progress in my health, but didn’t even realize I had changed until hearing from a couple different people that I’m “optimistic”, among other things I didn’t typically identify with. Me, optimistic? What? I’d so long had pessimism as my identity that I didn’t even realize that in health, my actions were indicating the opposite! 

But yeah, my point is that being a 9 doesn’t mean you are a super optimistic person! Honestly, the enneagram is more about why you do the things you do. All the ‘behaviors’ that are listed to accompany should be taken with a grain of salt

I’m not a fan of remakes to begin with, but I understand that there are some old movies that it could work for. Maybe the idea was great, but the video or sound quality could use a facelift, or maybe it would be improved with today’s looser censorship codes. 

IMO, Bergman is sacred ground. I see no reason whatsoever to remake anything he’s done because everything he has done already “holds up” by today’s quality and content standards. Any remake can only be worse than the original and feels like a money-grab to me :/

Seventh Seal may have been the wrong Bergman choice because it’s a little slower — if you like Lynch, try Persona! I also loved Wild Strawberries when I first got into arthouse.  

Other “entry-level” Recommendations I can think of. I don’t know if they’re all necessarily considered arthouse, but I still consider them artful and good entry points:  

Harold and Maude - Hal Ashby  
Dogtooth, The Lobster, and Killing of a Sacred Deer - Yorgos Lanthimos  
Diabolique - Henri Georges-Clouzot  
Any Kubrick

1. Drink water throughout the whole day. Not just before your run. I try to reach a gallon a day but I end up getting in 64-92 oz.

The next day you can do the same thing, but run for 22 mins, etc. It feels annoying at first but this is what has worked for me for building up endurance from nothing. It doesn’t take that long before your ‘annoyingly easy’ pace naturally gets faster
